uncited: - **Defocus Blur at Boundaries:** Using an all-in-focus depth map causes high pixel weights for rear objects near front object boundaries, even if blur degrades image quality.
- **Approximation Error:** Using mid-point approximation for $N_i$ in $L_{sight}$ is less accurate than using the CDF.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of sampling points per ray and the number of pixels.
If the scene is uniformly in focus and defocus blur is not a concern, standard depth losses may suffice.
Robust Depth Supervision was introduced in the context of differentiable holography and neural radiance fields.
